solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Mum arrested in tragic error goes on, quietly matter-of-fact

indicators.note: in an across clue, the quiet letter goes on the front of what follows it

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly

indicators.note: Mum is held, as if under arrest, inside the reworked letters
an error suggests the word tragic is set down wrongly, its letters jumbled

parts.note: Mum is a mother, MA

explanation.surface: A grieving mother caught up in some dreadful mistake carries on, calmly and without fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrested' looks like police business, but it only means held inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone pragmatic deals with things in a practical, sensible way, just as a matter-of-fact person does.

clue.text: Explore best on radio

indicators.note: on radio means as heard in speech, so the word for best is taken by sound

parts.note: a plum job or role is the best one

explanation.surface: Someone checking out the top stations on the radio dial.
explanation.definitionFit: To plumb is to investigate deeply, as a plumb line measures depth, so it means probe or explore.

clue.text: Checks outside, no-one turned up for screen tests

indicators.note: the checks word goes outside, around the other letters

parts.note: audits are official checks of accounts

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the letters run upwards, reversed

parts.note: no-one split as no plus one, with one as I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Inspections found nobody showing up for the film tryouts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no-one' is read as two pieces, NO and the Roman one.
explanation.definitionFit: Auditions are trial performances given by actors for a part, including screen tests for a film.

clue.text: 40-60 say, to be set up in commercial centre going forward

indicators.note: going forward means the centre word is placed at the front

parts.note: the centre is the middle

indicators.note: the turned letters sit in the commercial abbreviation

parts.note: ad is short for advertisement, a commercial

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the letters are raised, read upwards

parts.note: eg (for example) is the abbreviation for say

explanation.surface: Plans for a forty-to-sixty-storey development in a commercial centre are going ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' does double duty: it gives the wordplay's abbreviation and also tells us 40-60 is only an example of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Middle age is roughly the span of life from forty to sixty, so a person of those years is middle-aged.

clue.text: Fruit grower secures first class new apprentice

indicators.note: the tree secures, holding fast, the other letters inside

parts.note: a tree grows fruit
A1 means first class, written with the letter I for the figure one

explanation.surface: An orchard owner takes on a first-rate new apprentice.
explanation.walkthrough: A1, top quality, is written AI, the I standing in for the one.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainee is someone being taught a job or trade, which is what an apprentice is.

clue.text: Picks companion ring with small diamonds set in

indicators.note: the diamonds are set inside, like stones in a mount

parts.note: CH is Companion of Honour, a British order
O is ring-shaped
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: Choosing an engagement ring for a partner, with little diamonds set into the band.
explanation.walkthrough: The Companion of Honour is a British award; 'ice' is old slang for diamonds.
explanation.definitionFit: Choices and picks are both nouns for things selected from a range of options.

clue.text: Take care of supporters retiring with nothing

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the word for the supporters runs backwards

parts.note: tees support golf balls before they are driven
O is the round figure for nothing, zero

explanation.surface: Backers bowing out with nothing to show for it need looking after.
explanation.definitionFit: To see to something is a phrasal verb meaning to deal with it or look after it.

clue.text: Miliband is rising with Left perhaps

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the letters read upwards

parts.note: Ed Miliband, the British Labour politician

explanation.surface: The Labour politician gaining popularity with the political left.
explanation.walkthrough: Ed Miliband is a former leader of Britain's Labour Party, a party of the left.
explanation.definitionFit: Left is one example of a side, as in the left-hand side or the left wing in politics.

clue.text: Peer has some admirable qualities

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A member of the nobility possesses a number of fine traits.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer is someone of the same standing as another, so peer and equal are synonyms.

clue.text: Old inbox is corrupted by forums, regularly offensive

indicators.note: corrupted data is garbled, so the letters of inbox are rearranged
regularly picks every other letter of forums, the second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: An old email inbox is clogged with nasty posts from internet forums.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is corrupted' rearranges INBOX into BNOXI; 'regularly' takes OUS from fOrUmS.
explanation.definitionFit: Obnoxious describes something highly unpleasant or objectionable, the same as something that gives offence.

clue.text: Released around half of papers

indicators.note: half of the word around is taken, its last three letters

parts.note: ID, short for identification, means identity papers

explanation.surface: Someone let go after handing over roughly half of their documents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' looks like a word for approximately, but it is the word whose back half is used.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo a knot or catch is to unfasten it, so undid is a past-tense synonym of set free.

clue.text: Do a tour abroad including golf partner as a favour

indicators.note: the scrambled letters take the golf letter in among them
abroad here means astray or all over the place, so the letters of do a tour are scrambled

parts.note: G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet
N, North, is the bridge partner of South

explanation.surface: An invitation to go travelling overseas with a golfing companion, offered as a kindness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' rearranges DO A TOUR into AOODTUR; 'including' puts G inside it after the A, and N comes last. North and South are partners at the bridge table.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing someone a good turn means performing a helpful act for them, the same as doing them a kindness.

clue.text: Courage and audacity required for a hold-up

parts.note: bottle is British slang for nerve or courage
neck is British slang for cheek or audacity

explanation.surface: Pulling off an armed robbery takes nerve and cheek.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, 'bottle' means nerve and 'neck' means brazen cheek.
explanation.definitionFit: A bottleneck is a narrow point where traffic or work gets held up, a delay or congestion.

clue.text: Mutation in disease's unknown

parts.note: flu is a disease; the 's stands for has, joining it to the next piece
X is the classic algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A mutation in some illness has an unidentified cause.
explanation.definitionFit: Flux is a state of continual change, so it stands for alteration or mutation.

clue.text: Activewear clothing model taking cover under top photographer's raincoat

indicators.note: in a down clue, the cover word goes under the letter above it
clothing means dressing, so the rearranged letters wrap round the model letter

parts.note: the word splits as active, signalling an anagram, plus wear, whose letters are rearranged
the Model T was the classic Ford car

indicators.note: top picks the first letter of the word photographer

parts.note: a roof is a cover over a building

explanation.surface: A model in sports gear sheltering beneath a leading photographer's rain jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Activewear' hides its own anagram signal: 'active' stirs up the 'wear' fused to it. The Model T was Ford's famous car.
explanation.definitionFit: A waterproof is a British noun for a coat that keeps the rain out, such as a mac.

clue.text: Will validation for club come at last?

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for
a bat is a club used to hit a ball

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of the word come

explanation.surface: Asks whether getting a club's will approved will finally happen.
explanation.definitionFit: Probate is the legal process of proving a dead person's will is genuine before the estate is distributed.

clue.text: Rehearsed a scripted play

indicators.note: play suggests movement and looseness, so the letters of a scripted are rearranged

explanation.surface: A play with a script has been gone over in rehearsal.
explanation.definitionFit: Practised means having done something repeatedly to improve, as an actor who has rehearsed a part.

clue.text: Shock cleaner with fake crap

parts.note: a sham is a fake
poo is excrement, crap

explanation.surface: A product sold to treat electric shock turns out to be worthless rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: A shock is a thick mass of hair, not a jolt.
explanation.definitionFit: Shampoo is a liquid soap for washing hair, so it cleans a shock of hair.

clue.text: Gripe angrily about disgusting advantage of being wealthy

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go about, around, the disgusting word
angrily suggests a ruffled state, so the letters of gripe are thrown about

parts.note: vile means disgusting

explanation.surface: A furious complaint about the unfair perks of the rich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'angrily' rearranges GRIPE into PRIGE, which goes about VILE: PRI-VILE-GE.
explanation.definitionFit: Privilege is a special right or benefit available to a particular group, especially the rich.

clue.text: Romance ends after writer deleted number — harsh!

indicators.note: the novelist's shortened name comes before, and the ends follow it
deleted means the number letter is removed from the novelist's name

parts.note: Jane Austen, the novelist
N is the mathematical symbol for a number

indicators.note: ends picks the first and last letters of the word romance

explanation.surface: An exclamation at an author's romances ending after an issue is struck out.
explanation.walkthrough: The writer is Jane Austen, fitting the romance of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Austere means stern, severe and lacking comfort, a close synonym of severe or harsh.

clue.text: Snobbery's kindled by ones protected by English money

definitions.note: the 's is a joining is; the definition is snobbery

indicators.note: the inner letters are guarded on both sides by the outer letters

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for money, as in M3
lit means kindled, set alight
I is the Roman numeral one, so ones gives two of them, I's

explanation.surface: Snobbishness is stoked by those sheltered by old English wealth.
explanation.walkthrough: IS stands for I's, the plural of I, the Roman one.
explanation.definitionFit: Elitism is the belief that a select few deserve more, an attitude close to snobbery.

clue.text: Believes Charlie's wine is infused with tea primarily

parts.note: C is Charlie in the NATO phonetic alphabet; the 's is a joining has
red is a wine

indicators.note: the word is takes the tea letter inside it, as a drink is infused
primarily picks the first letter of the word tea

explanation.surface: Charlie's red wine has been steeped with tea, a strange drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' looks like a link word but is part of the wordplay, the container for the tea letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To credit a claim is to believe it, so credits is a present-tense verb meaning accepts as true.

clue.text: Designed insert to suppport cold water tank

indicators.note: in a down clue, the rearranged letters sit beneath and so support the cold letter

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: designed means arranged to a plan, so the letters of insert are rearranged

explanation.surface: An insert made to hold up a cold water tank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Designed' rearranges INSERT into ISTERN, placed under C.
explanation.definitionFit: A cistern is a tank for storing water, for instance in a loft or above a toilet.

clue.text: Variety of characters making a comeback in creepy tales

indicators.note: making a comeback says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A range of figures returns in a collection of spooky stories.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft gave the hiding no signal; 'in' is that signal, the letters lying inside 'creepy tales'.
explanation.definitionFit: A type is a style or font of printed letters, a set of printing characters.

clue.text: Checked fabric's unruffled when cutting out cape

definitions.note: the 's is a joining is; the definition is checked fabric

indicators.note: cutting out means removing the cape letter from the calm word

parts.note: placid means calm, unruffled
C is the map abbreviation for cape

explanation.surface: A tartan cloth stays smooth when a cape pattern is cut from it.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaid is a woollen cloth woven in a chequered or tartan pattern.

clue.text: Criticism over spritz cocktail winning award

indicators.note: over means covering, so the criticism word sits around the mixed letters

parts.note: to come under fire is to face criticism

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters of spritz are mixed

explanation.surface: A wine spritz drink earns harsh reviews despite an award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' means covering here: the criticism word wraps round the mixed letters rather than sitting above them.
explanation.definitionFit: First prize is the top prize given to the winner of a competition.

clue.text: Antelope's content in pasturelands

definitions.note: the 's is a joining is; the definition is antelope

indicators.note: content in means the answer is contained within the word that follows

explanation.surface: A grazing antelope is happy in the meadows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' looks like happy, but it is the contents of pasturelands.
explanation.definitionFit: The eland is a large African antelope with spiral horns.

clue.text: Taunt boy replacing original virtuoso in dance

indicators.note: the boy letter replaces, takes the place of, the opening virtuoso letter

parts.note: the jive is a lively dance

indicators.note: original picks the first letter of the word virtuoso

explanation.surface: A boy mocks the star performer by stepping in for them in a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacing' swaps V, the first letter of virtuoso, in JIVE for B.
explanation.definitionFit: A jibe is a mocking or insulting remark, the same as a taunt.

clue.text: Enquiry's beginning to pursue way various alibis balance

indicators.note: the opening letter follows, chasing, the other pieces at the end

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way

indicators.note: various suggests differing arrangements, so the letters of alibis are shuffled
beginning picks the first letter of the word enquiry

explanation.surface: An inquiry starts to chase down the varied alibis to weigh them up fairly.
explanation.definitionFit: To stabilise something is to make it steady, so it means to keep in balance.

clue.text: Singer Rita's holding back record for big musical production

indicators.note: the singer's surname holds the record inside it

parts.note: Rita Ora is a British pop singer; the 's stands for is

indicators.note: back means the record letters read in reverse

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A pop star is keeping a record back for a big stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: Rita Ora is a British pop singer; 'Singer' points to an opera singer but belongs to her name.
explanation.definitionFit: An opera is a large dramatic work set to music, sung throughout with orchestra.

clue.text: Duck down next to girl feeding deer

indicators.note: feeding means going into, so these letters go inside the deer

parts.note: a doe is a female deer

indicators.note: next to means the letter for down sits beside the letter for girl

parts.note: G is an abbreviation for girl

explanation.surface: A feathered duck lies beside a girl who is feeding a deer.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck or dodge is to avoid something by moving quickly aside, so both are verbs for evading.

clue.text: Bloke's life transformed by day in a Nottinghamshire town

parts.note: a bloke is a man, so bloke's gives man's

indicators.note: transformed means changed in form, so the letters of life are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man's life is changed by a single day spent in a Midlands town.
explanation.walkthrough: MANSFIELD is a market town in Nottinghamshire, an English county in the Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Mansfield is a sizeable market town in the county of Nottinghamshire, England.
